content: In chemistry, an incongruent transition refers to a phase change between two states of matter that is accompanied by a change in the chemical composition of the material. This is in contrast to a congruent transition, where the chemical composition remains unchanged during the phase change. Incongruent transitions can occur during processes such as melting, vaporization, or changes in allotropes (different structural forms of the same element). The concept of incongruent transition is also applied to related phenomena, such as the incongruent dissolution of a solid in a liquid solvent. This type of dissolution is commonly observed in geological processes. It is important to note that the term phase decomposition is sometimes used to describe incongruent transitions, but these transitions are characterized by being equilibrium processes. An example of an incongruent transition is incongruent melting, where a solid does not melt into a liquid of the same composition but instead forms a liquid and another solid phase with different compositions.
